Synopsis:
Dialog for one of the zombie beggars. After player talks to Father Carrion and has been tasked to kill them, they will react to this and either run to warn their leader, Thrumbo, or confront player. The following states are one-liners and hasmets for each possible quest state (meeting with thrumbo, outside house and inside father carrion's house once fully killed.)

Cluster Contexts:
- LOW_PhilgravesMansion_ZombieBeggar_Sacrum.json: The player has just met with Mystic Carrion and been drawn into his quest about runaway zombie beggars: recover the strays (or otherwise deal with them) in exchange for a Torch of Revocation. These lines come from one of those runaways — a standoffish, rotten‑smelling beggar who will either plead for coin, try to stand his ground, or flee to warn his leader Thrumbo depending on whether the player was told to kill or capture them. Off‑screen facts that matter: Thrumbo is the beggars’ leader (hiding in a wardrobe), Carrion is a mummy‑lord whose canopic jar is said to be hidden in Thrumbo (and destroying it can stop Carrion’s returns), and prior choices about accepting/refusing Carrion or killing him change later responses. The samples reflect the beggar’s mix of shameless begging, misplaced nostalgia, and pride in his duties to his “brothers.”
- LOW_PhilgravesMansion_ZombieBeggar_Morbus.json: These lines are spoken by one of Mystic Carrion’s runaway zombie beggars — a standoffish, childlike corpse you can smell from Carrion’s chambers — encountered after the player’s recent talk with Father Carrion about his “strays.” The beggar (Morbus/Lumbar) talks in a naive, obsessive way about a “sister who hides in the ground,” failing to grasp she’s dead, so player replies range from teasing to blunt attempts to break that delusion. Off‑screen states matter: you may have been tasked to recover or otherwise deal with the beggars (or to kill them), and the NPC may either flee to warn their leader Thrumbo, stand up to you, or later appear relieved if Carrion is defeated and the beggars occupy the house. Prior choices about accepting/refusing Carrion, killing him, or destroying his canopic jar (said to be hidden in Thrumbo) change these one‑line reactions and longer quest outcomes.
- LOW_PhilgravesMansion_Lumbar.json: The lines come from one of Mystic Carrion’s runaway zombie beggars — a servant the player has already met by scent in Carrion’s chambers. The player has just spoken with Father Carrion and been tasked (or otherwise involved) in dealing with his strays, so the beggar may react by fleeing to warn their leader Thrumbo or by cheekily confronting the player. Dialogue varies by quest state (meeting Thrumbo, scenes outside the mansion, or inside Carrion’s house after Carrion is fully dealt with) and reflects prior choices tied to the Torch of Revocation / canopic jar thread: whether Carrion was refused, killed, or his jar destroyed. Samples show the beggar’s rough, transactional personality (asking for gold to be hit, teasing the player) but other tone shifts (jovial vs. dejected) depend on how many beggars survived and how the Carrion quest was resolved.
- LOW_PhilgravesMansion_AD_BeggarsConversationEndState.json: The scene takes place after the party has permanently defeated Mystic Carrion and the zombie beggars have moved into Philgrave’s Mansion. When more than one beggar survived the encounter they’re in a light, joking mood — planning a party, cleaning out Carrion’s blood and guts, and treating Thrumbo like a steward. If only Thrumbo remains (because of how the player resolved the Carrion quest), he is quiet and dejected. Thrumbo is also the in‑house point of contact who can offer hints and is tied to the earlier Father Carrion choices and the Oskar’s Beloved / Torch of Revocation thread.
- LOW_PhilgravesMansion_Thrumbo.json: Thrumbo is one of Mystic Carrion’s runaway zombie beggars, hiding in a wardrobe after getting separated from three other “brothers” and waiting for them to turn up. Off‑screen, Carrion is a mummy‑lord seer in the Lower City who offered the player a deal (recover the beggars for a Torch of Revocation) and will repeatedly return from death unless his canopic jar is destroyed. If the player names Carrion, Thrumbo drops his street act—fearful and desperate—and admits Carrion’s canopic jar is hidden somewhere in Carrion’s house (he hints at a chamber beneath the salon). If Carrion isn’t mentioned, Thrumbo behaves like a normal, standoffish beggar (coughing, keeping his distance) to avoid attention.

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):
Sample 1:
- Narrator: *You recall where you've smelled this beggar's rotten musk before - in Mystic Carrion's chambers. This is one of the runaways he seeks.* (node 86)
- Strange Beggar Sacrum: Anything you can lend will be most gratefully received. (node 38)
- Strange Beggar Sacrum: Anything you can spare for a humble beggar? (node 19)
- Player: An ear, if you're willing to tell me your tale. How did you end up here? (node 23)
- Strange Beggar Sacrum: That devil, drink! I spent it all. || [context] NodeContext: Mournful, lamenting - a tad overdramatic (node 6)
- Strange Beggar Sacrum: All behind me, of course. Now I only require the gold for, ah, sustenance. || [context] NodeContext: Realises he's given away too much, collecting himself (node 52)

Sample 2:
- Narrator: *You recall where you've smelled this beggar's rotten musk before - in Mystic Carrion's chambers. This is one of the runaways he seeks.* (node 86)
- Strange Beggar Sacrum: Anything you can lend will be most gratefully received. (node 38)
- Strange Beggar Sacrum: Anything you can spare for a humble beggar? (node 19)
- Player: I'm sorry, my purse is rather light at present. (node 67)
- Strange Beggar Sacrum: Times are hard for us all. But we must persevere! || [context] NodeContext: Trying to make the player feel better (node 81)
- Strange Beggar Sacrum: My brothers are depending on me. || [context] NodeContext: Proud of the responsibility he's been given (node 48)

Sample 3:
- Narrator: *You recall where you've smelled this beggar's rotten musk before - in Mystic Carrion's chambers. This is one of the runaways he seeks.* (node 86)
- Strange Beggar Sacrum: Anything you can lend will be most gratefully received. (node 38)
- Strange Beggar Sacrum: Anything you can spare for a humble beggar? (node 19)
- Player: Earn your keep, beggar. The rest of us have to. (node 25)
- Strange Beggar Sacrum: I am trying! But people haven't the gold to spare, it seems. || [context] NodeContext: Doesn't want to believe people are so selfish as to not help him (node 50)
- Strange Beggar Sacrum: People were more generous in days gone by. || [context] NodeContext: Saddened, recalling his previous life (node 26)
